from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Heartbeat of Music", [
            "Music is organized by steady pulses.",
            "We group these pulses to create structure.",
            "This fundamental unit of time is a measure."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display steady pulse with glowing #FFD700 circle.
        pulse = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFD700", stroke_width=4)
        pulse.add(Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.6))
        self.place_at_grid(pulse, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(pulse))
        
        def pulse_updater(m, dt):
            m.scale(1 + 0.1 * np.sin(self.time * 2 * PI))
        pulse.add_updater(pulse_updater)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show waveform visual, emphasizing rhythmic regularity, #FFFFFF color.
        waveform = VGroup()
        for i in range(10):
            line = Line(start=UP*0.5, end=DOWN*0.5, color=WHITE)
            waveform.add(line)
        waveform.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(waveform, 'D2', 'D5')
        self.play(FadeIn(waveform))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Add metronome visual clicking on strong beats, #FF4500.
        metronome = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=0.8, color="#FF4500")
        needle = Line(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1, color="#FF4500").move_to(metronome.get_top(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        metronome_group = VGroup(metronome, needle)
        self.place_at_grid(metronome_group, 'B5')
        self.play(FadeIn(metronome_group))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup updaters
        pulse.remove_updater(pulse_updater)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Fractional Time Divisions", [
            "Notes represent specific fractions of time.",
            "A whole note equals the entire bar.",
            "Half notes split the whole in two."
        ])
        
        # Visual assets
        whole_circle = Circle(radius=1.2, color=WHITE)
        half_left = Sector(radius=1.2, start_angle=PI/2, angle=PI, color="#00FFFF")
        half_right = Sector(radius=1.2, start_angle=3*PI/2, angle=PI, color="#00FFFF")
        
        q1 = Sector(radius=1.2, start_angle=PI/2, angle=PI/2, color="#FF69B4")
        q2 = Sector(radius=1.2, start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color="#FF69B4")
        q3 = Sector(radius=1.2, start_angle=3*PI/2, angle=PI/2, color="#FF69B4")
        q4 = Sector(radius=1.2, start_angle=PI, angle=PI/2, color="#FF69B4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(whole_circle, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(whole_circle))
        self.play(
            FadeTransform(whole_circle, VGroup(half_left, half_right))
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        # Already split by halfs, represent whole note as reunification
        self.play(FadeTransform(VGroup(half_left, half_right), whole_circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF69B4")
        # Split into fourths
        self.play(FadeTransform(whole_circle, VGroup(q1, q2, q3, q4)))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Time Signature", [
            "Time signatures act like mathematical formulas.",
            "The top number counts beats per measure.",
            "The bottom note value defines the beat."
        ])
        
        # Initialize Equation 4/4
        time_sig = MathTex(r"{4 \over 4}", font_size=96)
        time_sig_group = time_sig.submobjects[0]
        top_num = time_sig_group[0]
        bottom_num = time_sig_group[1]
        
        self.place_at_grid(time_sig, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(time_sig))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # (Already written above via Write(time_sig))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        beats_label = Text("Beats per measure", font_size=24, color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(beats_label, 'C4')
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"),
            top_num.animate.set_color("#FF4500"),
            FadeIn(beats_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        note_label = Text("Note type per beat", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(note_label, 'D4')
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            bottom_num.animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            FadeIn(note_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Final visual: Pulse 1-2-3-4
        pulse = VGroup(*[Text(str(i), font_size=48, color="#FFFF00") for i in range(1, 5)])
        pulse.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(pulse, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        for i in range(4):
            self.play(Indicate(pulse[i], color="#FFD700", scale_factor=1.5))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Measure Theory in Action", [
            "We emphasize beats to create rhythm.",
            "Strong and weak beats define the groove.",
            "Accents follow patterns within the measure."
        ])

        # Define assets
        bar_line = Line(UP, DOWN, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=4).scale(1.5)
        notes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(4)])
        notes.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a bar line
        self.place_at_grid(bar_line, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(bar_line))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Grouping note symbols
        self.place_at_grid(notes, 'C4')
        self.play(FadeIn(notes))
        
        # Emphasize downbeat with a color pulse
        downbeat = notes[0]
        pulse = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FF4500", stroke_opacity=0.5).move_to(downbeat.get_center())
        self.play(FadeIn(pulse), pulse.animate.scale(1.5).set_stroke(opacity=0), run_time=1)
        self.remove(pulse)
        downbeat.set_fill(color="#FF4500", opacity=0.8)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Shift emphasis
        self.play(
            notes[0].animate.set_fill(color="#00FFFF", opacity=0.6),
            notes[2].animate.set_fill(color="#FF4500", opacity=0.8)
        )
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Universal Language", [
            "Music is sound arranged in time.",
            "Measure theory is the underlying architecture.",
            "We now understand the math of music."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        staff = VGroup(*[Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*2).shift(UP*i*0.2) for i in range(-2, 3)])
        notes = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE).shift(i*0.5 + UP*0.1) for i in range(-2, 3)])
        notation = VGroup(staff, notes)
        
        grid_geo = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.4, color=WHITE) for _ in range(9)])
        grid_geo.arrange_in_grid(3, 3, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(notation, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(notation)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(notation), FadeIn(grid_geo), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_in_area(grid_geo, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        grid_geo.set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(grid_geo), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Rhythm of Mathematics: Understanding Music and Measure Theory
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in music theory and STEM

sections.title: Introduction: The Heartbeat of Music
sections.content: Define 'Measure' as the basic unit of time in music. Introduce the concept of a 'pulse' (the steady beat) and how we organize these pulses into groups to create structure.
sections.example: Visualize a metronome ticking while a robotic dog taps its paw perfectly in time to the 'pulse'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Fractional Time Divisions
sections.content: Before understanding bars, we must understand note values. A 'whole note' acts as a circle (the whole), while half/quarter/eighth notes represent fractional divisions (1/2, 1/4, 1/8).
sections.example: A circular pie chart animation splitting into equal slices as a rhythmic pattern plays, showing how 4 quarter notes fill one 'whole' bar.

sections.title: Defining the Time Signature (The Mathematical Formula)
sections.content: Explain the time signature (e.g., 4/4). Top number = beats per measure; Bottom number = the type of note that gets the beat. This is essentially a fraction that dictates the 'math' of a bar.
sections.example: A digital display overlaying a sheet music score, showing 4/4 as a container that can only hold a sum of '1' (e.g., 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1).

sections.title: Measure Theory in Action: Grouping and Emphasis
sections.content: Explain 'Strong' and 'Weak' beats. Explain how measure theory allows composers to create 'Groove' by placing accents on specific fractions of the measure.
sections.example: A drum kit animation where the bass drum (strong beat) lights up in red and the snare (weak beat) lights up in blue, forming a repeating cyclical pattern.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Universal Language
sections.content: Summarize that music is simply 'sound arranged in time.' By understanding the mathematics of the measure, we move from just hearing music to understanding the architecture behind it.
sections.example: A final visual of a complex orchestral score collapsing into a simple, elegant geometric grid that highlights the recurring mathematical patterns.
